News.title: Tributes paid to TV presenter Dermot Murnaghan
News.content:
Broadcasters and politicians have paid tribute to TV presenter Dermot Murnaghan, who has died a year after he revealed he had been diagnosed with stage four prostate cancer.

The former BBC, ITV and Sky News journalist was 68.

"It is with great sadness that the family of Dermot Murnaghan announces that he passed away at home in North London earlier this morning," his family said in a statement posted to his X account. "He died peacefully with his family at his side."

A fixture on British TV news across five decades, he presented flagship programmes including the ITV Evening News and the BBC News at Six and Ten.

Murnaghan was a main presenter of BBC Breakfast from September 2002 to December 2007 and also hosted quiz show Eggheads.

After revealing his diagnosis last summer, he became an outspoken advocate for men to get tested for the condition.

"Needless to say my message to all men over 50, in high risk groups, or displaying symptoms, is get yourself tested and campaign for routine prostate screening by the NHS," he said.

"Early detection is crucial. And be aware, this disease can sometimes progress rapidly without obvious symptoms."

His family thanked the public "for the many, many kind messages of goodwill that he received over the last year since his diagnosis of Stage IV prostate cancer and his subsequent campaigning to raise awareness for screening programmes for the disease".

Common prostate cancer symptoms can include needing to urinate more frequently, particularly at night; difficulty starting to urinate, weak flow and it taking a long time; and blood in urine or semen. However, there may be no sign or symptoms for years.

News.title: Lorry driver arrested as child dies in collision
News.content:
Police have appealed for witnesses after a boy who was struck by a lorry died in hospital.

The collision happened in Epping Road, Chipping Ongar, Essex, at about 16:40 BST on Friday.

Officers arrested the lorry's 48-year-old driver, from Derbyshire, at the scene on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving.

He was released on bail until September while an investigation continued.

News.title: Dog rescued from Ben Nevis suspected to have eaten discarded cannabis
News.content:
A dog has been rescued from Ben Nevis after it is suspected to have fallen ill from eating discarded cannabis.

Christina Bluhme, a dog trainer from Esher in Surrey, was halfway up the UK's highest mountain when her black Labrador Tokyo collapsed on the trail.

Lochaber Mountain Rescue Team came to their aid and stretchered Tokyo down from the 4,413ft (1,345m) peak to a local vet.

Bluhme said Tokyo had made a full recovery after the incident during a trip to Scotland last weekend. She said vets believe she ingested cannabis left on the trail.

The dog trainer said "I genuinely thought I was going to lose her", after Tokyo lost the use of her legs and began drifting in and out of consciousness.

News.title: Letters reveal climber's last messages home before fatal Everest ascent
News.content:
Legendary mountaineer George Mallory wrote to his mother to say "the ink has begun to freeze" before he disappeared on Mount Everest in 1924, newly-discovered letters have revealed.

The writings record his first sight of the world's tallest peak, which he described as "a terrible formidable mountain", and include efforts to reassure his family with the words "I shall take every care I can".

Mallory, who was born in the Cheshire village of Mobberley, died during the expedition in 1924 and his body was missing for 75 years.

His great-nephew Bill Newton Dunn, 84, said his wife had found the letters, "a precious family archive", in a box secured with a pink ribbon.

"The letters mean a lot to me because they mention my grandmother [Mallory's sister] Mary, so it's a precious family archive and these are historical documents, so its important that they are well-looked after when they are sold," he said.

The letters, alongside photographs and an ice axe thought to have been used by Mallory were auctioned off by Sotheby's earlier this week.

News.title: Teenager charged with murder after off-road bike crash
News.content:
A teenager has been charged with murder following a fatal crash between a car and an off-road bike.

Police were called to Pen Cae Crwn Road, in Gorseinon, Swansea, at about 13:00 BST on Thursday, where a man was pronounced dead.

Tyler Ford, 18, from Morriston, has been charged with the murder of Ceiran Evans, also 18, from Gorseinon, following the incident.

He has also been charged with attempted murder of a second man - a 19-year-old who remains in hospital - and is being held in police custody.

South Wales Police said formal identification had not yet taken place but the family of Ceiran Evans is being supported by specially trained officers.

Four other men arrested as part of the investigation are on police bail. They are:

An 18-year-old man from Gorseinon arrested on suspicion of murder and Section 18 grievous bodily harm with intent.

A 33-year-old man from Gorseinon arrested on suspicion of murder.

A 38-year-old man from Gowerton and a 38-year-old man from Mount Pleasant arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

Det Ch Insp Danielle Thorne, from South Wales Police, said the investigation was "continuing at pace" and appealed for anyone with information on the incident to come forward.

She added: "We are aware of social media footage circulating from this incident, and we once again ask that this is not shared for obvious reasons. "

News.title: Master of coin: Trump made a fortune on his crypto business — thousands of investors lost their shirts
News.content:

President Donald Trump rang the opening bells of the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq exchanges remotely from the Oval Office Monday morning to tout the launch of “Trump accounts,” which will use federal money and private donations to start newborns off with $1,000 in savings.

But the dynamics of that move — the country’s first billionaire president leveraging his financial experience to help the masses — could not be more at odds with the unprecedented crypto enterprise Trump and his sons have been running over the last year.

Trump, who called Bitcoin a “scam” back in 2021, made more than $1.4 billion through his family’s own cryptocurrency venture in 2025, while hundreds of thousands of everyday investors in the venture lost their shirts. It was the president’s most profitable year ever across any business in his multi-decade career.

Fatime Elrgdawy, a 29-year-old software project engineer from California, told Reuters she lost more than $1,000 in savings on one $TRUMP coin play last year. At first she thought, “Oh my God, this is brilliant,” she told the news wire, but within five months her $2,000 investment was worth less than $120.

Still, she told Reuters, she considers herself lucky compared to other more heavily invested $TRUMP buyers into a meme coin that lost 97% of value from its January 2025 peak.

open image in gallery A crypto exchange office in Hong Kong with a screen featuring US President Donald Trump on March 12, 2025. ( AFP via Getty Images )

The Trump family launched its main crypto firm, World Liberty Financial, in the fall of 2024, in the final throes of Trump’s third presidential campaign. The move came after months of candidate Trump’s overtures to the industry, such as promising to fight for a national Bitcoin reserve. The crypto bosses seemed pleased, with billionaire executives backing the Trump campaign and the crypto industry emerging as the top sector donating in the 2024 elections.

Their faith in Trump and his Republican allies was soon rewarded. Bitcoin hit an all-time high in 2025, and the Trump administration drastically scaled back efforts to police the industry and stop crypto scams, while pardoning convicted fraudsters.

The Trump family, meanwhile, did even better.

Four days before Trump was inaugurated, an Abu Dhabi royal’s company secretly bought nearly half of World Liberty Financial, steering $187 million to Trump family entities, The Wall Street Journal reported. It was a striking transaction — a foreign authoritarian buying into a U.S. president’s family business — given World Liberty’s egalitarian mission to “democratize a new financial system.”

That same week, Trump unveiled a meme coin featuring an image of his triumphant fist pump after surviving the assassination attempt in Butler, Pa. The coin made him about $636 million last year.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump at the Treasury Department's Trump Accounts Summit on Jan. 28. The federal government will deposit $1,000 into investment accounts for every child born between 2025 and 2028 once parents sign their children up while filing their income taxes. ( Getty )

Trump investors haven’t been so lucky.

Roughly two-thirds of those who bought Trump’s meme coin have lost money, according to crypto data firm Nansen. As of late June, their losses totaled $3.81 billion. Another Nansen analysis, drawing from a smaller pool of data, finds that 85 percent of buyers in one of World Liberty’s tokens are in the red.

Civilian investors lost billions betting on Trump; political and financial elites backing his crypto, meanwhile, have had abundant good fortune.

The UAE, one of whose rulers bought into World Liberty, got approval last year to import highly coveted, advanced American AI chips. During negotiations, an employee at one of the royal’s investment firms reportedly held a job at World Liberty at the same time, the New York Times reported.

Another of the royal’s firms, MGX, which used $2 billion in a World Liberty coin in a recent investment, is now among the owners of TikTok’s U.S. operations, after the Trump administration spent months pressuring the social media company to spin off an American subdivision.

Asked for comment, the Trump administration told The Independent there are “no conflicts of interest” regarding his business activities. The Independent has also contacted the companies mentioned in this article for comment.

Trump, meanwhile, has described himself as being in the dark over the nature of his newfound crypto fortune.

“I could know about it,” Trump told CNBC last Thursday. “I didn’t. There’s nothing illegal. There’s nothing wrong with it.”

Meanwhile, prices for Trump’s meme coin and one of his World Liberty tokens have plummeted, part of a larger “crypto winter” of drooping prices across the entire sector.

No matter though, at least for the man in the Oval Office. As the president’s financial disclosures show, no matter what part of a financial cycle is underway, in the world of Trump and crypto, it pays to be at the top.

News.title: Wimbledon 2026 LIVE: Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev clash in final after Linda Noskova’s emotional tribute
News.content:
Sinner powers past Djokovic into Wimbledon final - Zverev next

Jannik Sinner plays Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final with both players looking to claim different back-to-back titles. World No 1 Sinner is attempting to win consecutive Wimbledons, while newly crowned French Open champion Zverev looks to back up his maiden success from last month’s Roland Garros.

Sinner, 24, has dominated Zverev in their recent meetings and has won nine matches in a row against the second seed. But the big-serving German, 29, has appeared to have been released by ending his long wait for a grand slam title at last month’s French Open, a tournament Sinner was knocked out of after just the second round.

The Italian returned to form with a ruthless thrashing of Novak Djokovic in the semi-finals, while Zverev ended the fairytale run of British wildcard Arthur Fery. Zverev’s first Wimbledon final is clouded by domestic abuse allegations that have marred his career, and which he has always strenuously denied.

On Saturday, Linda Noskova dedicated her victory over Karolina Muchova to her late mother, Ivana, who passed away on the eve of the same tournament two years ago. Noskova, 21, won her first grand slam title and became the latest Czech player to lift the Venus Rosewater Dish as she overcame compatriot Muchova in a thrilling three-set battle.

Tokito Oda successfully defended his Wimbledon crown with a dominant 6-1 6-1 win over Britain’s Alfie Hewett in the men’s wheelchair singles final.

The 20-year-old has now drawn level with Hewett with 10 grand slam singles titles and is joint-second on the all-time list, behind 28-time winner Shingo Kunieda.

Between them the pair have won the last 14 majors but the rivalry has become increasingly one-sided, with Oda winning 10 and Hewett four, and the Japanese star beating Hewett in eight of the 10 finals the pair have contested.

Oda, who is also the reigning Olympic champion, said: “I'm feeling incredible. When I won here the first time, I was 17 and I didn't know what kind of special place it is here. It's been three years since then and every year I come here, I play with pride and pleasure.

“Wheelchair tennis is growing and people are loving wheelchair tennis. I really appreciate your support and everyone who makes this possible [to play] on Court One - thank you everyone.”

Hewett had break points in Oda’s opening service game but was unable to take them and then fell down an early break, serving three double faults, before the Japanese player ran away with the opening set.

He picked up where he left off in the second set, breaking twice early on, and went unchallenged as he sealed his sixth consecutive grand slam title.

Hewett and fellow Briton Gordon Reid defeated Oda and his partner Gustavo Fernandez on Saturday to win a seventh doubles title as a team, but Hewett could not replicate their exploits on Sunday.

open image in gallery Oda is now a 10-time grand slam champion at the age of just 20 ( Getty )

The 28-year-old said: “Right now, I'm extremely disappointed. I was on a high yesterday, it was an incredible match with Gordon, and this match won't overshadow that performance.

“It's not the performance I wanted today, I don't think Tokito read the script! Congratulations to him and his team, that’s three grand slams now [in 2026] so I know what his goal will be going into the US Open. Hopefully someone can stop him!

“He's a incredible player and demonstrated that again today, so massive congratulations.”

It was a second defeat in the Wimbledon final in a row for Hewett, who won his only title thus far at SW19 in 2024.

News.title: Two men charged with murder after body found dumped in Kent woodland
News.content:

Two men have been charged in connection with a murder in south-west London after a man’s body was found in woodland in Kent.

Joshua Miller, 32, of Kingfisher Court, Wimbledon, was arrested on Friday and charged on Saturday with murder and preventing an unlawful burial, the Metropolitan Police said.

Jamie Cooper, 27, of the same address, was also arrested on Friday and charged on Saturday with preventing an unlawful burial.

Police received a report of a potential murder at an address in Kingfisher Court, off Queensmere Road, at around 10.55pm on Thursday.

No one was found at the property during a police search but officers believed someone had “come to harm” at the address and launched an investigation, the Met said.

On Friday, officers found the body of a man in a wooded area of Borstal in Kent.

The victim and the two men charged were known to each other, the force said.

The man’s next-of-kin were notified and are being supported by specialist officers.

Both Miller and Cooper were remanded in custody and will appear at Medway Magistrates’ Court on Monday, the Met said.

A third man who was previously arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender has been bailed.

News.title: Norway coach dismisses Fifa verdict on controversial England equaliser: ‘It’s pretty clear’
News.content:
Norway coach Stale Solbakken has dismissed Fifa’s verdict on England’s World Cup quarter final equaliser, insisting it was “clear” the ball hit overhead camera equipment in the build up to the goal.

The Norway bench was furious after claiming a goal kick from their goalkeeper deflected off a Spidercam cable and landed at midfielder Elliot Anderson’s feet, before he began the move that led to Jude Bellingham making it 1-1.

Fifa said there was “no evidence” the ball had hit the cable, pointing to data recorded by a chip inside the ball which they say suggested there was no contact.

However, Solbakken refused to accept Fifa’s version of events in his post-match press conference, saying: “I think it’s pretty clear that it did [hit the cable].”

Jannik Sinner bids to defend his Wimbledon title against second seed Alexander Zverev as the newly crowned French Open champion attempts to win back-to-back grand slam titles.

World No 1 Sinner, 24, reached his second consecutive Wimbledon final by beating Novak Djokovic in straight-sets and is one win away from a fifth grand slam title in total.

Zverev, who ended the run of British wildcard Arthur Fery in the semi-finals, is through to his first Wimbledon final and is enjoying his best run of form of his career.

The 29-year-old German ended his long wait to win a grand slam title last month at the French Open and appears to have been released by finally winning a major title.

Sinner and Zverev previously contested the 2025 Australian Open final, with the Italian winning in straight sets, which is one of nine consecutive victories in their head-to-head.

When is Jannik Sinner v Alexander Zverev?

The Wimbledon men’s final will begin from 4pm BST on Sunday 12 July.

How to watch Wimbledon on TV

In the UK, every match from Wimbledon will be available to watch live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website, with viewers able to access a stream from all 18 courts. In the US, ESPN and Tennis Channel hold the rights.

Jannik Sinner has won nine matches in a row against Alexander Zverev and has not dropped a set against the German in his last six victories against him. Before Sinner’s winning streak, Zverev had won four of their first five matches, including twice at the US Open. Sinner won 6-3 7-6 (4) 6-3 in a one-sided Australian Open final in 2025, for what was his third grand slam victory. This will be their first meeting on grass.

What has Jannik Sinner said about Alexander Zverev?

“We saw how aggressive he's playing, serving very big. He is a tough player to play against. He was before but now even more because of this confidence he has. When you start to win a lot of matches and don't lose a lot, it shows that he is playing incredible tennis. His confidence is good. He's very relaxed on court at the moment. But it's going to be very, very tough, very different than all the other matches we have played.”

What has Alexander Zverev said ahead of Wimbledon final?

“Once you win a major you know how to do it and you feel like you can do it again. You have this feeling inside of you. The second thing, I feel like I worked on my game a lot. I feel like my game has improved. Sometimes in sports it's as simple as that. You can talk about mental stuff, you can talk about certain situations, coaching changes, whatever. But if you improve as a player and you make the decision as a player to improve, you're going to do better in tournaments.”

News.title: Bellingham shapes World Cup to his will to secure England’s place in semi-finals
News.content:
England know World Cup quarter-finals well. This will be their 10th appearance in the last eight and it’s a running theme for many a fan that when asked to predict how the side will do heading into the tournament, to respond: “we’ll get the the quarters and then who knows...”

After Monday’s thrilling 3-2 win over Mexico, however, hopes are such that exiting in the quarter-finals would now be considered at best a hugely underwhelming result, at worst a failure.

The victory at the fabled Azteca had everything – at high altitude against a passionate, partisan crowd as much as the Mexico players, then down to 10 men producing a backs-to-the wall second-half performance that will live long in the memory. The result, other than getting the side into the last eight, is that expectation has risen. Added to that England will face Norway, a team that few predicted would get this far.

But this is the Norway of Erling Haaland and Martin Ødegaard, talented players who having caused Brazil a host of problems in the 2-1 win last round, are more than capable of doing the same to England tonight.

So, how did Thomas Tuchel gee up his players, knowing that victory in Miami will put England one match away from a first World Cup final since 1966? Well, he compared the win over Mexico as being like an FA Cup victory away at Sunderland in January.

“That was how we framed it with the team, it’s just you find a way to win. If you need a picture from the Premier League, it is January. It’s Sunderland, FA Cup. It’s away in Sunderland, it’s away in Leeds. You go. It’s adversity. It’s not good weather. You don’t like the decisions of the referee. Everything feels bad. They are on the front foot. You just need to get it done,” the England manager said.

“If you want to be at Wembley in the end. Don’t go out in January, don’t go out in February. No one will ask you any more how you did it. And then comes the exciting times. Then comes April, then comes May, things can become easier and then you have your identity and you have to let go.”

While the framing might be slightly left field, the sentiment is spot on. England have played well, in parts, to get to this point, but that will count for nothing if Haaland and Co get the better of them tonight.

Stay here for all the build up and action, with kick-off set for 10pm.

News.title: Lionel Messi stands in England’s way – this is how they can beat Argentina
News.content:
The biggest obstacle facing England is the smallest player on the field. Messi is playing with a purpose and passion that has terrified each of his opponents at this World Cup, and he comes into the semi-final having scored eight goals and assisted two in six matches so far.

England must accept that Messi will produce a handful of magic moments. He simply cannot be kept quiet for an entire match. The challenge is to react to those moments when they come, and then to hope for some luck.

In their quarter-final, Switzerland provided a helpful blueprint for England to follow. The Swiss kept the ball well, when they had 11 men, and slowed down the match with their patient passing. They also congested the areas in front of their penalty area, forcing Messi into deeper and wider positions.

Messi still registered an assist, from a corner, and created six chances. He also took four shots, the joint-most in the game, and completed the joint-most dribbles, with three. Overall, though, Switzerland will feel they contained him relatively well.

…but he also presents an opportunity

For all Messi’s threat, his presence in the Argentina team also represents an opportunity of sorts. So far at this World Cup, the 39-year-old has shown little willingness to do any defensive work off the ball. He usually conserves his energy when the opposition have possession, as the other outfielders work hard to cover for their captain.

Switzerland realised the potential here, with midfielders Xhaka and Remo Freuler able to use the additional space to work the ball around central areas and draw the sting from Argentina’s attack. Declan Rice and Elliot Anderson may have a similar opportunity in the semi-final.

Beware the other attackers

Until extra time of this semi-final, Argentina’s other high-profile forwards had failed to excel at this tournament. Alvarez, especially, had been quiet. His spectacular winning goal against Switzerland marked a timely return to form and will boost his confidence ahead of the semi-final.

News.title: Wales resurgence intact despite defeat by Argentina in Nations Championship
News.content:
The Welsh resurgence just about remains intact, but as far as the winning sequence goes, the red-shirted triumphant march was stopped at two as Argentina delivered a reality check in their five-try victory.

Yet it says something about the challenge facing Steve Tandy’s men that they were probably relieved that the scoreboard was not even more lopsided after they were second best for so long in this Test at Estadio San Juan del Bicentenario in San Juan.

With 20 minutes to go, the Pumas were on the brink of running amok, as so many of the Welsh opponents have been in the last three years as Wales amassed a record losing sequence – 18 – and compiled a trio of successive Six Nations wooden spoons.

But after coming on strong in the latter stages to defeat Fiji on the opening weekend of the Nations Championship, so the Welsh knuckled down and ensured the Pumas could not feast on their remains in the final quarter.

They might even have nicked two bonus points with a try at the end and, in truth, considering the fact Wales missed 31 tackles to Argentina’s eight, that would have seemed almost fantastical.

Yet as profligate as Argentina no doubt were, they were fully worthy of what should just about constitute a moral-boosting success after their disappointing home loss to Scotland seven days before.

But after five tries in the first 60 minutes, the Welsh were clearly there for the slaughtering. Overwhelmed at the ruck, they allowed so many line breaks and expended so much energy.

Wales enjoyed a wonderful start when Dewi Lake crashed over in the fourth minute from a driving maul. They had enjoyed superiority in this facet against Fiji, but against those old arch-masters of the art, this felt significant.

News.title: Scotland give Boks a much tougher game than England
News.content:
A true hallmark of a world champion outfit is their ability to hang tight in the scrappy moments. South Africa were far from perfect in this absorbing contest and boy were they made to work in this absorbing 10-try thriller.

For large parts of this contest, Scotland were tenacious and asked all sorts of questions of Rassie Erasmus’s experimental side. They were physical on both sides of the ball, looked more than comfortable in multi-phase passages of play and were rewarded for their patience and perseverance.

They picked up a try-bonus point in Pretoria, a city 1,339 metres above sea level, for their efforts, but they will leave wondering if it could have been more. To put their doggedness into context, this was Scotland’s highest points tally in South Africa. If anything, the altitude energised them, but they could not deliver the knockout blow.

South Africa needed a late Jesse Kriel score to seal their win in a match where their 42-28 scoreline somewhat flattered them. The hosts looked to have killed off the visitors with two quick-fire tries from Elrigh Louw and Damian Willemse in a high-octane second-half.

It should have sucked any remaining air out of Scottish lungs, but Gregor Townsend’s troops responded magnificently with two of their own through Josh Bayliss and Ben White to make it a seven-point game and set up a pulsating finish.

Telegraph Sport analyses the best moments in an enthralling Test match.

Wiese’s carry in the build-up to Roos’ try

Against South Africa, the world champions who battered England last week in their back yard, Scotland were always going to face a daunting challenge. Rassie Erasmus had boldly made 10 changes to the side that put Steve Borthwick’s side to the sword. One of those was lock Cobus Wiese, whose mind-boggling carry from the restart after Embrose Papier’s opening try was sensational. The 116kg lock was hoisted into the air by Boan Venter, with the prop showing incredible strength to keep Wiese stable. Replays, though, show Venter took a step or two forward while still carrying Wiese, before placing him back on terra firma with such force that the lock went on a rampage before offloading to Paul de Villiers. Was it completely legal? You cannot physically carry or run with an airborne team-mate forward into contact, which is considered dangerous play. There could easily have been a boot in someone’s face had Scotland’s chasing defence been closer and Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu can be seen waving his arms in protest as Wiese is brought down. Moments later, Evan Roos crashed over.

News.title: Noskova overcomes second-set collapse to win Wimbledon women’s title
News.content:
When Noskova led by a 6-2, 5-2 scoreline, and held three match points on the Muchova serve, some of the fans in Centre Court might have been making pointed remarks about value for money.

At that stage, the match was only around 70 minutes old, after the 57-minute “double bagel” inflicted by Iga Swiatek on Amanda Anisimova last year. The questions over equal pricing with the men’s final were on the point of resurfacing.

But Muchova took advantage of some tightening in Noskova’s racket arm by saving match points in three successive games, and then finally moving ahead via a marathon game that saw Noskova fend off six break points in her own right.

Noskova’s body language at this stage was understandably agitated. She turned to her coaches and held her arms out, as if to say “What am I supposed to do here?” But she worked wonders to regather herself for the decider, and finally completed the job with a note-perfect service game. The first-time grand-slam finalist cut a dejected figure, head sunk into her towel after being broken late on in the second set. She would be all smiles some 49 minutes later though after sealing the title.

Noskova’s victory was not just a brilliant tennis match but an advert for a broader perspective on life. So many professional athletes – especially tennis players – never make it beyond the narrow confines of their hotel rooms and tournament lounges. Whereas Noskova used her last off-season to travel to Zanzibar, the small island off the coast of Tanzania, and volunteer in a school for disadvantaged children.

News.title: Pollock and Caluori shine for England but woeful Fiji provide scant resistance
News.content:
“That’s the big thing. It’s been a bit of a re-set. Obviously getting the travel out of the way is a bit of an added challenge with the lay-out of the tournament but it’s been good. By the team we landed everyone was pretty tired so we didn’t have any meetings until that evening. It then becomes quite a quick turnaround when you land on the Monday. We had a big review of the South Africa game and the key takeaways from that...but a lot of what of what we would want to improve from South Africa is what we would emphasis around Fiji anyway.. I think that’s a really good place to be and for us to start off our week.”

In the immediate aftermath of the loss to the Springboks, both George and vice-captain Ellis Genge claimed that England had “rattled” the Springboks for an hour of the contest at Loftus Versfeld despite falling into a 17-0 deficit. George doubled down on this assessment, even if he described England’s start as “unacceptable”.

He also pointed out that many of the penalties that England conceded were a result of huge Springbok pressure, especially led by flanker Paul De Villiers at the breakdown. The challenge for England is to reduce their penalty count against Fiji without compromising their aggression.

“With regards to discipline the thing that is key to differentiate is there are penalties we give away but there are also penalties that opposition teams put us under too much pressure and that is then a penalty,” George said. “We have gone through the penalties and said Tommy Freeman in terms of his penalty, he knows he needs to lower his tackle height. That is a penalty that is not where we want to be, then there are some penalties that you give…De Villiers that time over the ball with the kicking strategy they had, that is a different type of penalty we gave away. So, that is a strategic and tactical point we need to make sure we get.

“With regards to our discipline, the big focus is just make good rugby decisions that allow you to keep your edge, keep your physicality and keep playing a game in a combative way which is when we are at our best. We have been disciplined in the past and we will be disciplined in the future, it is just about making sure we make better, more informed decisions but keep backing ourselves to put ourselves as close to the fire as possible.”

Sports.title: Switzerland stars slams ‘one-sided’ ref versus Argentina with England fans already fearing semi-final will be ‘rigged’
Sports.content:
SWITZERLAND players are the latest to hit out at World Cup refs after being beaten by Argentina – fuelling conspiracy theories that Lionel Messi’s side are still getting preferential treatment.

The 2022 winners are through to the semis after a 3-1 win in extra-time – but it wasn’t without controversy yet again as they now prepare to face England on Wednesday.



Swiss forward Breel Embolo was sent off with 20 minutes left of the quarter-final after he was shown a second yellow card for diving.

VAR checked the incident when Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes had been booked for fouling Embolo with the scores level.



And with new power to overturn decisions made through mistaken identity, Embolo was punished for going down without contact.

Had the ref not booked Paredes then VAR would not have been able to recommend an on-field review.

And it was Paredes who Embolo fouled for his first-half card as well.

Portuguese ref Joao Pinheiro showed Embolo another yellow following the dive and dismissed him to the horror of the Swiss players.



They surrounded Pinheiro and protested angrily but could not change his mind.

The game went to extra-time and Argentina eventually found a winner thanks to Julian Alvarez’s stunning long-range strike.

WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

But the manner of the loss incensed former Manchester City defender Manuel Akanji and his team-mates.

An emotional Akanji said: “When you have the referee against you, it becomes difficult. Every little thing was called against us.



“Every dive and every foul by the Argentinians went unpunished. I don’t usually say anything against the officials, but I’ve never experienced such a one-sided game as today.

“As soon as the game was over, I thought: ‘I’m so proud of our team.’

“What we’ve achieved throughout the entire tournament, and especially today.

“We played against the world champions, and they didn’t stand a chance.

“I can’t recall a single scoring opportunity from open play where we were lucky.



“If the game had continued 11 against 11, it would have likely gone in our favour.”

This is not the first time refs have been singled out for decisions made appearing to help Argentina, with some claiming that they are being pushed towards another title.

Many felt Messi was lucky to avoid a red card in the group stage opener against Algeria when he stepped on Aissa Mandi’s leg half an hour in.

Messi went on to get a hat-trick and has starred for Argentina despite Folarin Balogun being sent off for a similar tackle in the USA‘s last-32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina – although that was suspended thanks to Donald Trump.



And Akanji, now at Inter, was not the only Swiss player to feel let down.

Team-mate Remo Freuler said: “We had high hopes and put in a superb performance until the red card.

“That, of course, disrupted our flow. I still don’t understand how VAR can intervene in such a situation. Fifa needs to explain that to me.”



And boss Murat Yakin added: “After the equaliser, we clearly had the momentum on our side.

“Unfortunately, this was punished by a refereeing error. The referee shouldn’t have given the Argentinian a yellow card in that situation.

“There’s no reason for it; the incident wasn’t malicious or rough or anything like that.

“Then he corrects his own mistake and punishes us. That’s incomprehensible and beyond my comprehension.

“The decision is baffling to me, there was no reason for it. It’s a shame. We missed a great opportunity, and unfortunately, the journey is over.



“It hurts, but we can be proud. These are my great heroes.”

National captain Granit Xhaka also protested, saying: “The rules are the rules, we can’t change them.

“But with a decision like this, they’re killing football, that’s my opinion. I appeal to you: Don’t kill the game!”

This follows Egypt’s fury at being knocked out by Argentina in the last-16.

They lodged a formal complaint against Uefa ref Francois Letexier of France and pushed for him to be stripped of any remaining matches.



The African giants were fuming after having a goal disallowed in the second half when they were 1-0 up – although they would go on to make double the lead shortly after anyway.

And then the Pharaohs couldn’t believe it when Enzo Fernandez’s stoppage time winner was allowed to stand.

Egypt felt there had been a foul and a potential penalty at the other end moments before.

Manager Hossam Hassan said: “If they want Argentina to win this World Cup so badly why go to the bother of calling everyone else to come and play in it?”

The Egyptian FA added: “We cannot remain silent.



“Several key incidents raised serious concerns and left profound questions about the consistency and fairness of decisions that directly influenced the course of the game.

“Egyptian football has always respected the principles of fair play, sporting integrity, and respect for the game.

“These same principles require that all teams compete on equal terms and receive equal treatment.



“What occurred during the match has understandably generated widespread frustration among our players, staff and supporters about the serious refereeing mistakes and double standards.

“It is clear there were blatant errors with the VAR insisting on not reviewing some of the footage.

“We have demanded the exclusion of the referee and the entire officiating team from the World Cup after investigating these mistakes and the crime of discrimination against the Egyptian national team.”

Goalscorer Mostafa Zico went on: “We were all upset. Everyone can see why.

“After I scored to make it 2-0 every decision went against us – every decision.



“I still can’t see why my other goal was ruled out.

“We never thought we had won the game, not when you are playing for the World Cup against the holders.

“We made some mistakes but we did not deserve to lose that way.”

And Hassan said the game had been “rigged.”



They are not the only people to express that the tournament has been set up for Argentina, who now play England in the final four.

Three Lions fans are worried that they will be playing more than just 11 players in that game.

Some pointed out inconsistency with Djed Spence being denied a pen in extra-time against Norway compared to Nicolas Tagliafico getting one for Argentina in the Egypt clash from the same position.

And even the ref’s use of new mistaken identity laws have caused debate with questions over if VAR should have been able to intervene.



The BBC’s rules chief, Dale Johnson, explains that something was not right: “Mistaken identity is a factual offence which does not involve the use of the monitor.

“Changing a yellow card to a dive is a subjective change of decision, hence monitor use. So not mistaken identity.”

It has left supporters fearing the England vs Argentina semi – with many fans claiming the tournament has been “rigged” to help the reigning champions.



One wrote online: “England will destroy them unless the referee helps Argentina again, they have been playing so bad in this World Cup against small teams and even needing the referee’s help to win, I just don’t see how they can beat England without the referees.”

Another said: “England have to be so careful on Wednesday. The referees are going to do everything they can to get Argentina to the final. They’ve been doing it the entire World Cup, they’re not going to stop now.”

A third commented: “Let’s see what FIFA and the referees, who have favored Argentina so far, will do against England.”

And head coach Thomas Tuchel has voiced his concerns around the refs as well, saying after the Mexico clash: “It’s not good enough

“He [the referee] can send any team out in any moment. It’s just not good enough.



“It’s just erratic, it’s just unreliable in matches. Now we have two fourth officials who just scream at you if you put one foot out of a coaching zone. It’s just not good enough.”

Sports.title: Ex-England star claims Jude Bellingham making Gazza look ‘AVERAGE’ after another sensational World Cup rescue act
Sports.content:
JUDE Bellingham is dragging England towards the World Cup final one rescue act at a time and the comparisons with Paul Gascoigne are becoming impossible to ignore.

The Real Madrid superstar struck twice as the Three Lions came from behind to beat Norway 2-1 after extra time, taking his tally to six goals for the tournament and booking a blockbuster semi-final with Argentina.



It was another night when England needed someone to seize the moment and, once again, Bellingham answered the call.

Former England defender Jamie Carragher believes the 23-year-old has now gone beyond even Gazza’s iconic Italia ’90 campaign.



Writing in the Telegraph, Carragher claimed: “Jude Bellingham has been so good at this World Cup that he is making Paul Gascoigne’s performances at Italia ’90 look average.”

He quickly clarified it was no slight on the England legend, adding: “That is not intended to disparage Gazza.



“It is a compliment to an outstanding young player who is having more impact at an international tournament than any English footballer who has preceded him.”

For more than three decades, Gascoigne’s displays in Italy have been viewed as the benchmark for an England player at a World Cup.

His dazzling runs, fearless skill and unforgettable tears after the semi-final defeat to West Germany cemented his place in football folklore.

WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS



But while Gazza captivated a nation, Bellingham is doing something even more valuable – deciding matches.

Against Norway, he hauled England level in first-half stoppage time before reacting quickest to score the extra-time winner and send Thomas Tuchel’s side into the last four.

It continued a remarkable pattern throughout the tournament, with Bellingham repeatedly stepping up when England have needed him most.

As Carragher put it: “Bellingham is starting to specialise in rescue acts.”

The former Liverpool defender also argued no England player has ever produced a better World Cup across six matches, pointing out Bellingham has already set a new England record for goals from open play at a single tournament.



What makes the run even more remarkable is that only weeks before the World Cup, Bellingham was not even guaranteed a place in Tuchel’s strongest XI after the England boss experimented with other attacking midfield options.

Instead of shrinking under the pressure, Bellingham has embraced it.

His swagger, authority and ability to decide football’s biggest matches have become the driving force behind England’s charge, with Harry Kane the only player to rival his influence.

Carragher even compared Bellingham’s mentality to Steven Gerrard’s, arguing the midfielder possesses the self-belief to walk on to any pitch convinced he belongs among the very best – whether lining up against Erling Haaland, Lionel Messi or Kylian Mbappe.

England are now just one win from a first World Cup final since 1966.

And if Bellingham continues producing moments like these, Carragher believes there will soon be no debate over where he ranks among England’s all-time greats, concluding: “By the end of his career, Bellingham will have that honour.”

The opening 1-0 win over Haiti had the Tartan Army dreaming of the knockout phase but defeats to Morocco and Brazil left hopes hanging by a thread.

The midfielder has achieved superstar status since swapping Man Utd for Napoli almost two years ago.

And it’s fair to say he’s been making the most of it!

The former Manchester United ace has been spotted out and about at the World Cup this summer.



And he was also at Wimbledon last month, sat in the Royal Box.

The 115-cap international never played in a World Cup semi.

This will be Kane’s second – along with two Euros finals.

Sports.title: BBC’s 3D cam shows England goal should have been DISALLOWED in World Cup win over Norway despite Fifa’s spidercam claim
Sports.content:
THE controversy surrounding Jude Bellingham’s crucial equaliser against Norway has taken another dramatic twist after BBC’s 3D replay appeared to show the ball changing trajectory moments before England scored.

The incident occurred just before Bellingham fired home the equaliser in first-half stoppage time during England’s 2–1 World Cup quarter-final win in Miami.



Norway’s players immediately protested, claiming the ball had clipped one of the overhead spidercam wires from a goal-kick in the build-up.

Under the Laws of the Game, if the ball touches an external object such as an overhead cable while in play, the match should be stopped and restarted with a dropped ball – meaning Bellingham’s goal would not have counted.



FIFA swiftly dismissed those claims after the match.

World football’s governing body said: “We have checked the data and there was no peak on the graph from the connected ball heartbeat sensor.”



FIFA later added there was “no evidence” the ball had touched the overhead cable before England’s equaliser.

But fresh pictures from the BBC’s 3D tracking replay have now reignited the debate.

The replay appears to show a noticeable deviation in the ball’s otherwise smooth flight at the exact point where the spidercam cable was positioned, before play continued and England launched the move that ended with Bellingham finding the net.

The footage has led to renewed questions over whether the ball did in fact make contact with the cable, despite FIFA insisting its connected-ball technology detected nothing unusual.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

Norway and Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard admitted after the game that “margins were not in our favour”, while Fulham midfielder Sander Berge branded the incident “ridiculous” as the Scandinavian side questioned the officials’ decision.

The controversy ultimately mattered little to England, who completed a comeback through Bellingham’s second goal in extra time to seal a 2-1 victory and book a World Cup semi-final showdown with Argentina.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick considering shock tactical tweak to ease Man Utd midfield crisis with summer transfer in limbo
Sports.content:
MASON MOUNT is prepared to occupy a deeper role at Manchester United to ease their midfield crisis.

United only have one fit senior central midfielder in Kobbie Mainoo after Casemiro was released and Manuel Ugarte ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament at the World Cup.



The £35million deal to sign Ederson from Atalanta is in doubt but United sources denied reports from an Italian reporter on Friday that the move is off.

United have agreed a £50m deal with Chelsea for 22-year-old Andrey Santos, who made 13 Premier League starts last season.



Mount started in midfield in United’s goalless draw with Sunderland and 3-0 victory at Brighton in May.

United originally bought the 27-year-old from Chelsea in July 2023 to partner Casemiro even though Mount is a playmaker by trade.



Mount’s positive impact towards the end of last season has effectively safeguarded his future and United head coach Michael Carrick values his work rate and versatility.

England international Mount is set to start United’s pre-season schedule in midfield as Mainoo will not report for pre-season until the club’s Dublin training camp starts on August 9.

Mainoo has not played a single minute across England’s six games at the World Cup and Thomas Tuchel sent on right back Reece James to play in midfield in the quarter-final win against Norway.

Late call-up Nathaniel Chalobah, the Saudi Pro League-based Ivan Toney and Mainoo are the only outfield players yet to appear for England in the United States and Mexico.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

There is precedent for tournament participants linking up with the United squad earlier than scheduled in pre-season.

Newly-signed Fred did not appear for Brazil during the 2018 World Cup and linked up with his new team-mates before his mandatory three-week break had ended.

United will come under pressure to finalise deals over the next week, with their first pre-season friendly against Wrexham in Helsinki on Saturday.

Club sources insist deals for Ederson, Santos and free agent Karl Darlow remain possible.

Seventeen of Santos’ 25 starts for Chelsea last term came after Liam Rosenior was appointed in January.



Santos played for Rosenior on loan at Strasbourg in one of his four loan spells away from Chelsea.

United considered bringing in Darlow, 35, four years ago and he started 22 times for Leeds United last term.

Ederson, 26, made two substitute appearances for Brazil at the World Cup and United had always aimed to finalise that planned signing in July.

Sports.title: Inside England’s amazing World Cup win over Norway, from Beckham singing Wonderwall to Bellingham and Tuchel
Sports.content:
JUDE Bellingham’s brilliant brace sent England into the World Cup semi-finals – but the Real Madrid star’s heroics were only half the story on a dramatic night in Miami.

Thomas Tuchel’s side came from behind to beat Norway 2-1 after extra time and move to within one game of a first men’s World Cup final since 1966.



But from a bizarre spidercam controversy to a rare public disagreement between manager and matchwinner, there was plenty to unpack after the final whistle.

England looked to be heading for another frustrating night when Andreas Schjelderup’s dipping effort gave Norway the lead before half-time.



Bellingham dragged the Three Lions level in stoppage time before pouncing on a goalkeeping error early in extra time to book a blockbuster semi-final against Argentina, who beat Switzerland 3-1.

However, his equaliser sparked immediate controversy.

The Norway players surrounded the officials, furious that a potential deflection off the overhead spidercam wire in the build-up had been missed.

Had it done so, play should have been stopped before Bellingham found the net.



Norway captain Martin Odegaard admitted “margins were not in our favour”, while team-mate Sander Berge branded the incident “ridiculous”.

But FIFA later ended the debate by revealing data from the connected match ball showed “no evidence” it had touched the overhead wire before England’s leveller.

WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

If the on-pitch drama wasn’t enough, Tuchel’s post-match interview quickly grabbed headlines.

Despite guiding England into the last four, the German admitted he was far from satisfied with what he had seen.



He told ITV: “The result is fantastic, we are in the last four – it’s amazing – but I’m not happy with the performance. We made life very, very difficult for ourselves… We were lucky today.”

Those comments did not appear to go down well with Bellingham.

When asked about his manager’s assessment, England’s two-goal hero initially replied: “Yeah, well, whatever. Whatever.”

He then defended his team-mates after battling through the sweltering Miami conditions.

Bellingham said: “Maybe he doesn’t know what it’s like to play in those kind of conditions against Erling Haaland, Martin Odegaard, Antonio Nusa and Alexander Sorloth.



“Sometimes you have to win dirty, and we’ve done that again tonight.”

Asked whether England had been lucky, Bellingham simply smiled and replied: “No comment.”

Tuchel later insisted there was “no disconnect” between himself and the squad, stressing he was simply demanding higher standards despite reaching the semi-finals.

Captain Harry Kane also backed his manager, revealing Tuchel congratulated the players but reminded them they still had another level to reach.



Post-match interviews aside, the response and behaviour of the England fans was brilliant.

England’s players headed over to the travelling supporters as Oasis anthem Wonderwall echoed around the stadium before thousands joined together for an emotional rendition of Hey Jude in honour of matchwinner Bellingham.

Among those belting out the lyrics was Sir David Beckham, with the former England captain spotted singing alongside son Romeo as England celebrated another memorable World Cup night.

And there was still time for one final moment of comedy.



John Stones repeated the prank he pulled after the win over Mexico by grabbing his shoulder during the celebrations, prompting worried looks from Harry Kane and Declan Rice.

Seconds later the Manchester City defender burst into laughter, shook it off and turned the fake injury into another celebratory dance.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

England are now just one win away from the World Cup final.

But after a night that delivered goals, controversy, dressing-room banter and a rare exchange between Tuchel and his star player, the Three Lions know Argentina will provide an even tougher test.

Sports.title: Switzerland rage at 'unacceptable' decision as Argentina profit from World Cup 'disaster'
Sports.content:
Switzerland rage at 'unacceptable' decision as Argentina profit from World Cup 'disaster'

Switzerland were left furious after their World Cup quarter-final defeat to Argentina, having been reduced to 10 men when Breel Embolo was shown a second yellow card

View 2 Images Switzerland were on the wrong side of a new law (Image: Rico Brouwer/Soccrates/Getty Images)

Angry Switzerland manager Murat Yakin has branded the new law which led to Breel Embolo's sending off against Argentina as 'unacceptable'. Swiss forward Embolo was shown two yellow cards, the second of came about in controversial circumstances.

‌



Referee Joao Pedro Silva Pinheiro initially booked Argentina's Leandro Paredes for a foul on Embolo, only for replays to show that there was no contact and that the Rennes star had dived. The referee was then instructed by VAR to review the incident on the pitch-side monitor and made use of a law which came into force ahead of the World Cup.

‌



With Embolo already on a yellow card, Pinheiro gave him a second booking to reduce Swizterland to 10 men just five minutes after Dan Ndoye had cancelled out Alexis Mac Allister's first-half goal. Yakin's side held on to take the quarter-final to extra-time before goals from Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez broke Swiss hearts.

‌



Post-match, Yakin fumed: "There was definitely no reason to award a yellow card. It was a harmless situation. He should have let play continue. We were punished because of a rule that is unacceptable.

"I don't understand it. ‌The fact that they intervened unnecessarily is extremely hurtful. It's a rule that has nothing to do ⁠with football. It destroyed our game today. We have to accept it, but it ‌is painful to lose that way."

‌



Meanwhile, Switzerland midfielder Remo Freuler described the decision as a 'disaster'. "I don't know what this referee is doing here," Freuler added.

"I don't know, I don't understand why they call it for a situation like this, because there were many fouls, made also in the first half, maybe he has to also to call them for a yellow card. So I don't understand. How can a VAR change a game with this situation?"

The flashpoint has prompted more accusations that Agrentina are being favoured by FIFA officials, having been on the right side of multiple key decisions in their dramatic last-16 victory over Egypt. "I wouldn't say they (Argentina) are being favoured," Yakin said.

‌



Do you agree with the new law? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Murat Yakin can't understand why the law was introduced (Image: JUAN MABROMATA/AFP via Getty Images)

"(But) football didn't come out on top, we were punished by a referee mistake. I didn't know this rule before; it's a very harmless situation, a yellow card was awarded, VAR interfered.

‌



"It was a very meaningful moment for us and it was decisive for the outcome of the match. The VAR and the ref... the fact that they introduced such a rule is just unnecessary. It's extremely hurtful - we missed this opportunity, we're not going to the semi-finals, but I think we deserved to be there."

Instead, it's Argentina who are in the last four. Lionel Messi and Co. will take on England in their semi-final clash on Wednesday in Atlanta at 8pm UK time.

Sports.title: Zlatan Ibrahimovic tears into England star as Thomas Tuchel's side left with 'one player less'
Sports.content:
Zlatan Ibrahimovic tears into England star as Thomas Tuchel's side left with 'one player less'

England beat Norway 2-1 after extra time in the World Cup quarter-finals, with Jude Bellingham scoring the decisive goal following a 1-1 draw at the end of normal time

View Image Noni Madueke struggled to make an impact for England against Norway (Image: Icon Sport via Getty Images)

Zlatan Ibrahimovic has ripped into Noni Madueke following his performance against Norway, suggesting England were effectively playing with 10 men. England went on to beat Erling Haaland's Norway 2-1 to book their place in the World Cup semi-finals.

‌



However, Madueke came under scrutiny after struggling to make an impact on the right wing. Early in the match, Elliot Anderson picked him out with a cross-field pass, but the winger could only send his delivery straight out of play.

‌



He also endured a frustrating afternoon in one-on-one situations, repeatedly failing to beat his full-back. At half-time, Ibrahimovic, who was on punditry duty for Fox Sports, did not hold back in his assessment of the 24-year-old.

‌



British Airways forces Norwegian Air into embarrassing Instagram post after World Cup defeat READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"They're playing with one player less so far. Madueke has been on the pitch," the former Manchester United striker said. "But I have to say every time he gets the ball so far he makes the wrong decision and he’s walking on the pitch.

"If I’m Thomas Tuchel, I change it because he's done nothing in this first 45. Even the hydration break didn't help him."

‌



Gary Neville also weighed in on Madueke's performance on the Stick to Football podcast, explaining why the winger's final ball repeatedly let him down.

"We had a coach at United called Jimmy Ryan, a really good technical coach," he stated. "Usually when a player doesn't cross the ball well, it's because their stride isn't right, their pacing running up to the ball.

"I think he's running too fast and doesn't slow himself down - he might be looking up too much, thinking he can pick someone out with a Beckham-style cross. On the run, at full pace, you've only really got three options: whip it in low across goal, pull it back low, or stand it up to the back post.

‌



"You've got to know which one you're choosing before you get there, concentrate on your stride, and make it like a pass. I think he's sprinting too fast to cross it well."

Neville then shared his view on what makes the world's best wingers so effective.

‌



"They say wingers are unpredictable, as if that's some kind of positive - but the best wingers are the most predictable players in the world," the ex-Manchester United captain added.

"Riyad Mahrez is going to cut back onto his left foot; [Mohamed] Salah is going to put it in the far corner; Thierry Henry’s finish from the left; David Beckham will take it out of his feet and whip it in. You know exactly what they're going to do, and you still can't stop it.

"As a winger, you have to be a bit more predictable - you've got to have two or three things you do brilliantly."

‌



Jude Bellingham scored both of England's goals as they came from behind to beat Norway 2-1, cancelling out Andreas Schjelderup's opener before netting the extra-time winner.

The Three Lions have discovered their World Cup semi-final opponents will be Argentina after Lionel Messi's side beat Switzerland 3-1 after extra time. The quarter-final had finished 1-1 at the end of normal time.

Sports.title: What Marco Rose will be told by Bournemouth hierarchy after replacing Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
What Marco Rose will be told by Bournemouth hierarchy after replacing Andoni Iraola

Marco Rose was the man the Bournemouth hierarchy turned to after the now Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola informed the club that he would be leaving

View 2 Images Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose during a pre-season training session at his new club (Image: (Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images))

Bournemouth are gearing up for their first ever European tour in 127 years, but Cherries striking legend Steve Fletcher has warned new boss Marco Rose that the Premier League must be their top priority.

‌



They finished an incredible sixth place in the Premier League, just three points behind the final Champions League qualifying place taken by Liverpool, who then snapped up Bournemouth's boss Andoni Iraola. The Cherries are now in the Europa League against the likes of AC Milan, Juventus, Bayer Leverkusen, Marseille and Real Sociedad.

‌



But Fletcher, speaking as MrQ celebrates becoming AFC Bournemouth's new official sleeve partner, believes it will be made clear that maintaining their top-flight status is the most important thing. Fletcher, who holds the club record with over 650 appearances, said: “That will be reiterated to everyone at this football club, whether you are a player or a staff member, because the Premier League is our bread and butter, and we can’t lose sight of that.

‌



“As much as Europe is going to be exciting and it will put us on the map, you can’t lose sight of what is the most important thing and that is the Premier League.

“This is the first time and it is a baptism of fire for us, but everyone at the football club will be doing everything they can to make sure we stay in the Premier League and we represent ourselves really well.

Declan Rice injury worries laid bare after Gary Neville and Ian Wright agree on England star READ MORE :

“We will try to better what we did last season. Is that a tough ask? Yes, it is, but is it possible? Yes, it is.”

Rose was one of three candidates considered by the Cherries, along with Kieran McKenna and Inigo Perez, to succeed Iraola. And Fletcher believes: “Marco Rose is the perfect replacement for Andoni because we are a football club who like to play a certain way.

“We like attacking football and we like pressing teams and are very energetic, so our recruitment director and sporting director, Tiago Pinto, would have looked at that and brought in a manager who can work with a group of players who did fantastically well last season.

‌



“Andoni was amazing for three seasons and deservedly gets a move to one of the biggest clubs in the world, but we have brought in Marco, who has been in for a few days already building up for the lads to come back. He’s been nothing short of fabulous already."

View 2 Images AFC Bournemouth club ambassador Steven Fletcher on the iconic Bournemouth beachfront as casino brand MrQ became the club's new official sleeve partner

The Cherries are set to travel to Manchester City on the first day of the new campaign, then host Everton, followed by a visit to Newcastle United, before Brentford and Liverpool visit the Vitality Stadium. Although the fixture list looks daunting on paper, Fletcher insists: “You can look at the fixtures and say we have a tough Christmas or a tough run-in, but it doesn't get much tougher than playing Man City away.

‌



"Sometimes, when you are a club like us, you need to catch these teams when they are not in full flow.

“Maybe back in the day when we first got in the Premier League back in 2015, we would look at when we were playing Liverpool, when we were playing Man City, Man United and Arsenal, but now I think it just rolls in, and now it is exciting to go to the Etihad on the first day of the season and play Man City.

“They will be looking to bounce back under their new manager and try to win the Premier League. So I think it is an exciting fixture, if anything, and then Liverpool as one of the first home games, but bring on the big clubs, as that is the whole point of playing in the Premier League and that is the excitement.”

Sports.title: Erling Haaland's dad rages after England beat Norway and lashes out at referee
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland's dad rages after England beat Norway and lashes out at referee

England came out as 2-1 winners over Norway after extra time in the World Cup quarter-final, thanks to Jude Bellingham's brace

View 2 Images Alfie Haaland was far from happy (Image: ITV)

Alfie Haaland, the former Leeds United and Man City full-back and father of Erling Haaland, has taken a swipe at the referee of England’s World Cup quarter-final win over Norway.

‌



The Three Lions needed extra time to book their place in the semi-final, after initially going behind in the first half. Jude Bellingham’s double, with the first coming just before half time and the second in extra time, saw England come out as 2-1 winners.

‌



The game was billed as Haaland vs Harry Kane, with Thomas Tuchel’s side managing to keep the Man City striker relatively quiet before he was surprisingly substituted during the additional 30 minutes. As ever, Alfie was in the stands to support his son, and he didn’t hide his feelings before and after the game.

‌



Lionel Messi sends message to England players with X-rated reaction after Argentina win READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The match was packed with talking points, with Kane feeling like he was fouled in the build-up to Norway’s opener. Norway's staff then claimed that the ball hit a cable before Bellingham’s equaliser.

In the second half, Norway had a goal ruled out after a VAR check, with Haaland shown to have pushed Elliot Anderson as they tusseled during a corner. There was another VAR intervention in extra time, when England saw a penalty overturned after a challenge on Djed Spence.

‌



In the seconds after the referee announced the decision not to award a penalty, the camera turned to Haaland snr, who appeared to turn to the England fans and do a diving gesture. He then sticks two fingers up in the same direction and appears to say “f*** off”.

The former Norway internation has continued to show his dissatisfaction. After the game, he took to social media and wrote: “Well done Bellingham and referee.”

View 2 Images Norway's Erling Haaland was unable to find the net vs England in the World Cup quarter-final. (Image: Liu Lu/VCG via Getty Images)

‌



Early on Sunday morning, he added: “Saved bye [sic] the referee. Hope you win the WC now. But feel we got robbed today.”

Some fans gave their response to his claims: “I’d genuinely love to know how they were ‘robbed’,” one said. “They had a goal disallowed for blatant foul. There was also an extremely debatable foul in the build up to their goal and the ref overturned a penalty for England??”

A second added: “I mean we had a clear penalty overturned mate. Wouldn’t say the ref favoured us at all.”

‌



“No, Alfie, you should be proud of your country,” a third said. “The boys gave everything they had and fought until the very end. Sometimes you just have to acknowledge that the other team was better on the day and accept it with grace.”

Alfie Haaland wasn't the only person associated with Norway to be unhappy with the referee. Winger Andreas Schjelderup also spoke out about decisions.

"Unfortunately, the margins were against us, the odds were against us," he said. "Some decisions by the referee were a bit bitter. If we lost fully it would have been a bit different."

‌



Captain Martin Odegaard also added that Norway "didn't get much help from the referee. The margins went against us and we had a bit of bad luck."

England will now take on Argentina in the semi-final on Wednesday night (8pm). Argentina came out as 3-1 winners over Switzerland after Extra time in the early hours of Sunday morning.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker makes Jude Bellingham feelings clear with huge England prediction
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker makes Jude Bellingham feelings clear with huge England prediction

Gary Lineker has made a bold claim about Jude Bellingham after he scored twice to help England beat Norway 2-1 in the quarter-finals of the World Cup

View 2 Images Gary Lineker thinks Jude Bellingham could become onf of England's greatest footballers (Image: Netflix)

Gary Lineker believes Jude Bellingham could be England’s 'greatest ever' footballer. The Three Lions now stand one win from their first men's World Cup final since 1966 after Bellingham scored twice against Norway.

‌



The Real Madrid star first cancelled out Andreas Schjelderup's dipping effort two minutes into first-half stoppage time. Bellingham then set up a mouth-watering final four showdown against Argentina when he pounced after Orjan Nyland failed to hold a shot from substitute Morgan Rogers at the start of extra-time.

‌



By scoring twice, Bellingham became the first player to do so in consecutive knockout stage games at a single World Cup since Diego Maradona in 1986 and 12 of his England goals have been at major tournaments. And Lineker said: “I would go as far as to say I think there’s a chance that I think he could well be, or end up being, England’s greatest ever footballer. And that is a big shout. We’ve had some really great players. Some of them have not necessarily done it for their country, others have.

‌



“Go back to people like Bobby Charlton obviously, I would say would have to be up there. You would put Harry Kane in that bracket and there are other players as well, but I think at this age, to be doing what he’s doing and to grabbing England by the scruff and getting them over the line, that is superstar.”

Agreeing with Lineker on the Rest is Football podcast, former England winger Joe Cole said: “He’s definitely in the conversation. I remember when he turned up when he was about 18 in the England squad, and I was talking to a few of the lads, Declan, people like that, and they were going, 'This kid’s unbelievable'.

“When you hear players talk about it, that’s when you know. The media can talk about it, the press can talk about it, everyone else can talk about it, but when the players who train with him every day are excited by him, that tells you something.”

Bellingham has now scored six times so far in the tournament, putting him alongside Lineker (1986) and Harry Kane (2018, 2026) as the only England players to score at least five times at a single World Cup.

And Gary Neville believes the way Bellingham does the “ugly bits” of the game are what have elevated the midfielder to the top.

‌



View 2 Images Jude Bellingham celebrates after England's win over Norway at the 2026 World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

“The reason he [Bellingham] elevates himself to world class isn't just the goals, it's the out-of-possession work, it's the interviews, it's what he did after the game today," he said on the Stick to Football podcast, brought to you by Sky Bet.

“That's the complete package for me. That is what takes you to a different level. He's not just a goalscorer or someone who delivers in big moments, he does the ugly bit.

‌



“Turning up for an interview after a draw against Ghana, that's the ugly bit, the bit you don't really want to do, but you do it anyway."

Sports.title: BBC's stance on sacking pundit and grovelling apology after ex-England boss vows to stay away
Sports.content:
BBC's stance on sacking pundit and grovelling apology after ex-England boss vows to stay away

Some BBC pundits have come under fire during the corporation's broadcasting of this summer's World Cup

View 3 Images Former England boss Sir Gareth Southgate snubbed working as a pundit for the World Cup (Image: Getty)

Being a pundit for a broadcaster like the BBC at a World Cup comes with its fair share of flak. So much so that former England manager Gareth Southgate has opted to steer well clear.

‌



ITV and the BBC have allowed fans back in the United Kingdom to enjoy what has been a memorable World Cup thus far. Guiding supporters through all the action from North America has been a crack team of ex-footballers and seasoned presenters.

‌



Some of English football's biggest names take to punditry after retiring, and covering a World Cup is the crème de la crème. But fans can be rather ruthless when mistakes are made or opinions are expressed.

‌



The BBC has made it abundantly clear how they deal with the kickback when it arrives and how they front up to their own errors. Though this hasn't prevented the likes of Southgate from refusing to mic up.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

Gary Lineker makes stunning BBC return after England World Cup victory READ MORE :

Wayne Rooney put on the spot in response to Erling Haaland message before England vs Norway READ MORE :

The backlash BBC pundits face

Supporters often pull no punches when they aim criticisms at pundits. For example, at this World Cup, the BBC employed Olivier Giroud as an analyst.

‌



View 3 Images Giroud struggled in his new role (Image: BBC)

The former Chelsea and Arsenal striker appeared earlier in the tournament, often for France matches, but fans were having none of it when he featured during Belgium's clash with Egypt, branding him "disastrous."

Such backlash, which is commonplace when ex-pros and broadcasters take to our screens, is one reason why ex-England boss Southgate swerved appearing on TV for the World Cup.

‌



He posted on Instagram before the tournament: "It's obviously a very different tournament for me this one, I've been at the last seven World Cups as a player, as a broadcaster, a scout and then as the manager.

"So this time I took a conscious decision not to do the TV. I didn't think it would be helpful for me to be talking about the team and I don't want anything to be misconstrued or thrown at them at press conferences, so best for me to keep out of the way."

How does the BBC react to the complaints?

The corporation is usually quick to front up to its own errors, though. Earlier during the World Cup, when France faced Senegal, a mistake with the line-up graphics showed a picture of French defender Dayot Upamecano in the place of Arsenal's William Saliba. Jules Kounde was also depicted as Ibrahima Konate.

‌



View 3 Images The BBC apologised for the error (Image: BBC)

Fans were outraged that the visual teamsheet had been displayed incorrectly, and the BBC issued a statement which read: "We apologise for this mistake."

However, when it comes to their pundits, they usually back them to the hilt. At the 2014 World Cup, Phil Neville, brother of current ITV pundit Gary, was part of the BBC's coverage.

Article continues below

During England's bitter defeat to Italy at the competition, Neville came under heavy fire for his commentary as he struggled. But the BBC's head of football at the time stuck by him, setting the precedent for how they likely deal with complaints volleyed in their direction.

"He had a bad night at the office," Mark Cole told The Independent. "He was really hurting that night when I spoke to him but he dusted himself down the next morning."
